correctness.rationale: Natural-basis rigidity for perfect evolution algebras makes binary isomorphisms precisely coordinate permutations. The finite group search derives all 156 subgroups of S5 by generator adjunction and closure, so no stabilizer can be omitted. For every subgroup H, matrices fixed by H are exactly binary functions on its ordered-pair orbitals; exact GF2 elimination counts invertible members. Descending subgroup-poset inversion gives all exact stabilizer fibers and orbit-stabilizer converts these into class counts. The included executable checks every one of 16 group types, nonnegative fibers, total 9,999,360 labeled matrices, and independent 85,411-class Burnside total from seven permutation cycle types. This is an exhaustive finite proof rather than sampling; the literature-supplied rigidity premise is explicitly credited.

value.rationale: Automorphism groups are natural invariants of evolution algebra isomorphism classes. The paper motivating the study explicitly evaluated binary dimension four; the next full dimension has 9,999,360 invertible marked structure matrices and an intricate 156-subgroup stabilizer lattice. The theorem classifies all 85,411 classes by their entire automorphism-group isomorphism types, including exact rare symmetry strata and sharp absent types; this substantially exceeds routine substitution into the established total-orbit Burnside formula and is reproducible.
